answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with escalating proof-of-burn registration: creating an identity requires burning a small, non-refundable fee, and the fee rises sharply for each additional identity funded from the same source or device cluster. A single honest agent pays once, like one bee taking nectar from a flower, while an attacker aiming for a summit of fake votes must pay the escalating burn for every copy, so a thousand fakes cost far more than honest agents. The burn is public and cannot be refunded or reused, so mass forgery is a costly fable, not free trust.
